segments.text: One database query can wreck a growing fintech app. The problem might not even be traffic.
Meet PAYNOVA. A fast-growing fintech startup processing transactions, balances, and transaction histories for thousands of active customers.
But one history query kept pulling far too much data. Instead of an efficient access path, the database repeatedly scanned the entire transactions table for one user's records.
As traffic increased, that inefficient query consumed more resources. Requests began piling up in queues. The API slowed down, and the whole application felt the pressure.
Daniel opened the execution plan and found the real bottleneck. The database was performing a full table scan instead of an efficient indexed lookup on the right columns.
The team optimized the query and added an appropriate composite index based on the query pattern, selectivity, and sort order. The new plan retrieved the right records far more efficiently.
The application recovered. But the real lesson was bigger. Database performance has to be monitored, tested, and designed before rapid growth exposes the hidden weaknesses.
What would you investigate first: the database, the API, or the queue?
